'''Philip Coppens''' (October 24, 1930 – June 21, 2017)<ref>{{cite web|author=Ellen Goldbaum |url=http://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2017/06/031.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170707083117/http://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/2017/06/031.html |title=SUNY Distinguished Professor Philip Coppens has died |publisher=University at Buffalo |date=June 23, 2017 |archive-date=July 7, 2017 }}</ref> was a [[Netherlands|Dutch]]-born American chemist and crystallographer known for his work on [[Multipole_density_formalism|charge density analysis]] using X-rays crystallography<ref>{{Cite web |last=Payne |first=Robin |title=Philip Coppens |url=https://history.amercrystalassn.org/h_coppens_memoir |access-date=2022-08-16 |website=history.amercrystalassn.org |language=en-us}}</ref> and the pioneering work in the field of [[photocrystallography]].<ref>{{cite journal | last=Coppens | first=Philip | title=The dramatic development of X-ray photocrystallography over the past six decades | journal=Structural Dynamics (Melville, N.Y.) | volume=4 | issue=3 | date=2017 | issn=2329-7778 | pmid=28191481 | pmc=5291789 | doi=10.1063/1.4975301 | doi-access=free | page=032102 }}</ref>

==Education and career==
The [[Amersfoort]]-born Coppens received his B.S. and Ph.D. degrees from the [[University of Amsterdam]] in 1954 and 1960, where he was supervised by [[Carolina Henriette MacGillavry|Carolina MacGillavry]]. In 1968, following appointments at the [[Weizmann Institute]] and [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]], he was appointed in the chemistry department at the [[University at Buffalo, The State University of New York|State University of New York at Buffalo]]. He was a SUNY Distinguished Professor and holder of the Henry M. Woodburn Chair of Chemistry. Among the many 3-dimensional structures Coppens characterized is the [[Sodium nitroprusside#Structure and properties|nitroprusside ion]].<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1021/cr000031c | volume=102 | issue=4 | title=Photoinduced Linkage Isomers of Transition-Metal Nitrosyl Compounds and Related Complexes | journal=Chemical Reviews | pages=861–884 | last1 = Coppens | first1 = Philip| year=2002 | pmid=11942781 }}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Coppens was a corresponding member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] since 1979<ref>{{cite web|author= |url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/3994 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304100654/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/correspondents/3994 |title=P. Coppens |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |accessdate=17 July 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> and a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] from 1993.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Goldbaum |first1=Ellen |title=Coppens Named Fellow of AAAS |url=https://www.buffalo.edu/news/releases/1993/12/3333.html |access-date=May 9, 2022 |publisher=University at Buffalo |date=December 3, 1993}}</ref> Additionally, he was awarded the [[Gregori Aminoff Prize]] of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in 1996, the [[Ewald Prize]] of the [[International Union of Crystallography]] in 2005,<ref>{{cite web | title=P. Coppens awarded the seventh Ewald Prize | website=International Union of Crystallography | url=https://www.iucr.org/iucr/ewald-prize/ewald07 | date=August 2005}}</ref> and [[Kołos Medal]] in 2013.
